content:
deploy-bot: Deploy started for client-sdk v3.4.0 -> canary group (10%) at 21:12 UTC :rocket:
incident-bot: ALERT: error rate spike observed on /streaming/paged endpoint (canary). 5xx rate 28% over baseline in last 2m. Paging backlog increasing. :rotating_light:
Alex: seeing tons of socket resets and frame header mismatches in the canary instances. logs: 
```
ERR: incoming frame header mismatch: expected FLAGS=0x01 got 0x03
Trace: conn=10.4.22.14 session=xyz
num_pending_paging_requests=428
```
Maria: confirmed. Repro on local repro harness with v3.4.0 client + server runtime v2.9 when concurrent paging > 200. Paging window appears to mis-handle continuation frames.
Sam: tagging oncall-runtime. @Alex are we sure it's client->server framing and not network MTU/path issue?
Alex: not MTU. I ran against same infra with v3.3.1 and it's fine, so regression in v3.4.0. Likely a header/enum change in streaming protocol.
Emily: Customer impact: we saw five active customers using streaming paging in canary bucket. Two reported elevated request timeouts via support. CS flagged one high-traffic customer (AcmeHealth) with production errors.
Jordan: rolling back the canary? We should flip kill-switch for the streaming-paging feature flag while we triage. That will keep rest of SDK changes in but stop paging code path.
Maria: I can kill the flag now (ff:streaming_paging_v3) — will that be non-disruptive? It toggles the client-side paging handshake to legacy mode.
Sam: do it. Also scaling canary nodes down/up might flush bad state but kill-flag quicker.
Alex: warning: because the change is in the client framing, toggling server flag might not protect clients that already negotiated. But it's worth it for new handshakes.
ProductOps: notifying impacted customers via status page and an outbound message to the account team for AcmeHealth. Draft message ready: "We're investigating intermittent streaming failures; temporary mitigation in progress."
Maria: kill-switch flipped at 21:16 UTC. Confirming new handshakes are legacy mode.
incident-bot: NOTE: feature flag ff:streaming_paging_v3 set to OFF by Maria at 21:16:08 UTC.
Alex: after flag flip, 5xx rate dropped to 6% in 3m window. Paging backlog reduced from 400+ to ~30. Looks promising.
Emily: support report: AcmeHealth is seeing reduced errors, but had 30% degraded latency for 10 minutes. They were on canary.
Sam: next step: roll back client release in canary and stop rollout to remaining buckets. @deploy-bot can you halt the rollout?
deploy-bot: Rollout paused by Sam at 21:20 UTC. No further traffic will be sent to new client instances.
Jordan: assigning follow-up: Alex and Maria to build a minimal repro, Sam to coordinate rollback plan, Emily to compile customer impact timeline, ProductOps to handle comms. Handoff to night on-call (Jordan) at 21:30 UTC.
Alex: repro steps posted in thread: 
1) start local runtime v2.9
2) run client v3.4.0 with 4 parallel paging streams each sending ~1000 tokens and randomly chunked frames
3) observe header mismatch in ~30s
```
# repro command
pytest tests/stream_paging/test_repro.py::test_frame_mismatch --concurrency 4
```
Maria: temporary hotfix ideas: restore old frame enum mapping in client OR add tolerant parsing on server to accept multiple enum variants. Tolerant parsing might be quicker but risky.
Sam: short-term: rollback canary to v3.3.1 clients and keep kill-switch off for new handshakes. Long-term: patch client and add strict integration tests for frame enums.
ProductOps: open postmortem ticket and include timeline + customer impact; subject: "client v3.4.0 streaming framing regression — kill-switch & rollback". Assign to eng-runtime and product.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: ticket INC-2107654321 created: "streaming-paging framing regression — canary impact". Severity P2.
Emily: CS updated customers at 21:25 UTC. Logged one escalation to priority support for AcmeHealth.
Jordan: handing off to night oncall. I'll monitor slack and paging channel. If error rate rises above 10% reopen the incident.
Alex: will follow up with a PR with a small client fix and test harness by EOD.
Sam: summary for handoff: ff toggled, rollout paused, rollback scheduled, customer comms sent, repro steps in thread, assigned owners.
ProductOps: will draft a public status message once rollback completes.
incident-bot: RESOLVE CHECKPOINT: 21:40 UTC — canary error rate stabilized under 10%; mitigation in place. Keep incident open for root cause and postmortem.
